meaning.evidence: Every instruction kept: three gallons, strain through muslin, overflow pipe, ten-gallon tank, two pet cocks, notch settings. Additions ("you'll blow your arse to kingdom come", "give you a hell of a whack") are colour on the original's warnings.

sense.evidence: Fits: "under its own steam", "the more grunt you get", "topped up", "Once the engine's properly loosened up" for limbered up.

authenticity.evidence: Natural Aussie plain speech ("make bloody sure", "dead sure", "beats hard water hands down"), with a couple of stock lines bolted on ("full stop").

register.evidence: Casual and clear but closer to level 3 than a level-5 yarn; long stretches are just plain paraphrase ("The system holds about three gallons."). Swearing ("bloody", "arse", "hell") within level 2.

tone.evidence: Still an instruction manual, with the cautions kept serious ("don't you dare, under any circumstances").

flow.evidence: Reads smoothly: "Keep pouring water in till you're dead sure the radiator and the cylinder water jackets are both full."

essence.evidence: Plainly the 1919 Ford starting checklist, Q-and-A shape intact.

register.evidence: Heavy on exclamations but the body is the untouched original ("Upon receipt of the car see that a supply of medium light, high-grade gas engine oil"); swearing within level 2.

flow.evidence: Broken joins: "Well, During the first few days", "gasoline'n air", "Anyway, under the steering wheel".

essence.evidence: Under the noise the manual is there, but it no longer reads as instructions anyone could trust.

B.summary: Rule-engine noise over an untranslated manual, with an outright mistranslation of draining the tank.

meaning.evidence: Every instruction kept with numbers and cross-references; additions are colour on the original ("it'll go up like a bonfire on cracker night", "that crank handle'll give your wrist a wallop").

sense.evidence: Exact: "chock-a-block" for full, "bungs up the little tubes", "Soon as the car rocks up" for upon receipt, "goin' flat out" for maximum speed.

authenticity.evidence: A real Aussie mechanic's voice: "get your mitts on", "be careful as", "quick smart", "suss out where they need to be".

register.evidence: A full level-5 yarn throughout, every section retold; swearing light ("make bloody sure", "flamin' volatile"), inside level 2.

tone.evidence: Still a careful how-to under the yarn: "And this is the big one: don't run the car under her own steam".

flow.evidence: Reads like it was written that way: "Pour the oil in nice and slow till it runs out the top cock."

variety.evidence: Very varied idiom, though "she"/"her" for the car and dropped-g forms recur a lot.

essence.evidence: Unmistakably the Ford starting checklist, retold by a bush mechanic.
